title: Make AppUser/AuthState/AuthUser @freezed instead of hand-rolled classes without value equality
why: AppUser, AuthState and AuthUser are plain hand-written classes (immutable, but no @freezed, no custom ==/hashCode), so two instances with identical field values compare unequal by reference identity — AuthState is literally the `state` type of a keepAlive Riverpod Notifier. Current consumers avoid the fallout by exclusively `.select()`-ing down to primitive sub-fields (e.g. `s.currentUser?.firebaseUid`, a String, in manage_tutors_providers.dart/app_shell.dart/persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart) rather than comparing whole AuthState values, so no concrete rebuild-storm is demonstrated today — but it is a landmine for the next `ref.watch(authStateProvider)` call that doesn't remember to add a `.select()`.
recommendation: Convert to @freezed (or at minimum implement value ==/hashCode) — low-risk given the classes are small and already immutable.
acceptance_criteria: AuthState(...) == AuthState(...) is true for equal field values (documents the fix via a unit test)
build_runner regenerates cleanly with no call-site breakage

corrections: The 'exclusively .select()-ing' claim is inaccurate: grep shows ~15+ sites (profile_providers.dart:23/79, app_shell.dart:140/152/453, sync_providers.dart, restore_providers.dart, settings widgets, etc.) do `ref.watch(authStateProvider)` on the whole object, not just the 3 cited select() sites. Practical risk stays low regardless since AuthStateNotifier only reassigns state on genuine transitions (checked auth_state_provider.dart _init), not superfluously — so P3 still holds, just not for the stated reason.

The 'why' claims consumers 'exclusively' .select() down to primitives, avoiding fallout. False: grep shows 18+ sites (sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:58, outbox_providers.dart:19/51/87, profile_switcher_sheet.dart:72, app_shell.dart:140/152/453, etc.) do `ref.watch(authStateProvider)` on the whole object with no .select(). This understates rather than overstates risk, so it doesn't undermine the finding or its P3 rating.
